# anxcloud_kubernetes_node_pool_network (Resource)

Resource to attach and update an additional VLAN network on a Kubernetes node pool.

The VLAN is managed independently and can be resolved with the `anxcloud_vlan` data source. Reconciliation error states remain readable so the attachment can be repaired with a later configuration update.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "anxcloud_vlan" "node_pool_network" {
  id = "existing-vlan-identifier"
}

resource "anxcloud_kubernetes_node_pool_network" "example" {
  name            = "storage"
  node_pool       = anxcloud_kubernetes_node_pool.example.id
  vlan            = data.anxcloud_vlan.node_pool_network.id
  bandwidth_limit = "1000"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Network interface name.
- `node_pool` (String) Identifier of the node pool to which the network is attached.
- `bandwidth_limit` (String) Network bandwidth limit identifier, for example `1000`.
- `vlan` (String) Identifier of the VLAN attached to the node pool.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Node-pool network identifier.
- `state` (String) Current reconciliation state identifier.
- `state_text` (String) Human-readable current reconciliation state.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String)
- `delete` (String)
- `read` (String)
- `update` (String)

## Import

Import a node-pool network using its identifier:

```shell
terraform import anxcloud_kubernetes_node_pool_network.example <identifier>
```
